verdict_reason: The BLME paper defines one Spearman correlation per head over the paired {i,j} observations and then a mean over heads, but the current code computes a separate Spearman for every query row and averages those row coefficients. On a valid causal attention head, current evaluate() returns +1.000000 while the paper-defined pooling returns -0.204614 on the identical off-diagonal pairs (-0.517866 if the diagonal is included); on live GPT-2 tensors the two estimands are -0.212799 and -0.391167, an absolute difference of 0.178368.
comparable_reason: On a fresh same-passage fp32 panel of 6 local models, the shipped raw key has Spearman rho=+0.836660 with n_layers (p=0.037841), +0.925820 with d_model (p=0.008050), and +0.885714 with parameter count (p=0.018845). The nosink twin reduces those associations to +0.478091/+0.493771/+0.657143, but fails the required causal test: adding zero-output identity attention blocks leaves logits bit-identical (max delta=0.0) while both raw and nosink move -1.000000 -> +0.750000 from 1 to 8 layers, with rho(depth)=+1.000000 for both.
github_reason: Inspection of both official repositories found 0 implementations of a distance-versus-attention Spearman: RoFormer releases the Q/K rotation and attention product, while ALiBi releases the linear distance bias added before softmax. There is therefore no original metric code to cross-run; against an independent tie-ranked row census, BLME does match its own rowwise algorithm exactly (absolute difference 0.0 on 36,432 live GPT-2 rows), but that is not GitHub reference parity.
paper_reason: RoFormer Section 3.4.3/Figure 2 publishes a bound term for RoPE inner products and ALiBi publishes perplexity results, but the two papers publish 0 values of this trained-attention Spearman; the BLME paper likewise gives only its formula and qualitative negative-sign hypothesis. Thus neither the live GPT-2 rowwise value -0.212799 nor the pooled value -0.391167 has a published scalar target.
confounds_reason: Architecture dependence is causal, not just correlational: a function-preserving insertion of 7 zero-output attention blocks changes raw and nosink from -1.000000 to +0.750000 with max logit delta 0.0, and the 6-model live panel gives raw rho=+0.925820 with width. Position-0 off-diagonal mass also spans 0.098188-0.516944 (5.26x), correlates +0.771429 with the raw key but only +0.142857 with nosink; the current fp32 promotion closes the tested dtype channel to 0.235% raw on Pythia-70M, so dtype does not explain these architecture effects.

NORMALIZED TWIN: mean_positional_decay_correlation_nosink fails the strict mechanism test. With identical logits (max delta 0.0), inserting zero-output identity attention blocks moves it -1.000000 -> +0.750000 over 1 -> 8 layers and gives rho(depth)=+1.000000; its improved 6-model correlations (+0.478091 depth, +0.493771 width, +0.657143 parameters) are therefore fit evidence, not architecture invariance.

CONFIG/PROTOCOL ONLY, not part of verdict: the effective merged default is num_samples=5 and evaluate() caps every passage at 256 tokens even though the paper says long-context only. CODE STATE RESTORATION: model.float() casts buffers as well as parameters, but finally restores only parameters. A direct bf16 model test restored the parameter to torch.bfloat16 while leaving a registered bf16 buffer as torch.float32; Pythia-70M happened to retain an identical full state digest because its relevant buffers were already fp32.

DTYPE COVERAGE: fp32 attention promotion is disabled above exactly 2,000,000,000 parameters, leaving 2.8B/6.9B/12B-class low-precision models on the old numerical path. This is unverified on those large models; on the permitted Pythia-70M test, the repair is effective: bf16 versus fp32 raw differs by 0.000614485 (0.2351%), nosink by 0.000662576 (0.2319%), with 0 flat and 0 non-finite scored rows and exact parameter-state restoration.
